title: Notable recent biology and biomedicine papers — arXiv announcement batch 2026-11-18
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart, and its biomedical preprint coverage is incomplete; this is an inferred ranking from available evidence, not readership or download data.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: The latest available configured biology/biomedicine listings yielded 12 selected papers for the 2026-11-18 announcement batch. The strongest recurring pattern is computational methods reconstructing or predicting biology, with a smaller bridge to experimental measurements. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance-and-evidence ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage, not measured popularity.

sections.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
sections.abstract: Abelio structures AI-driven hypothesis generation and refinement; its PEG and cholesterol-anchored complementary-DNA proposals were tested in damaged Caco-2 intestinal epithelial monolayers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that complementary DNA caused sequence-specific, reversible barrier-readout changes; their PEG experiments found effects depended on membrane-surface configuration.
sections.unique_caveat: Biological evidence is in vitro in Caco-2 cells; the proposed membrane geometries were not directly visualized, and scientific-soundness scoring partly uses an LLM judge.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: q-bio.QM cross-list; benchmarked on 50 curated research objectives against four frontier LLMs, with two AI-proposed approaches tested in cell monolayers.

sections.title: Discovery of new antiviral agents through artificial intelligence: in vitro and in vivo results
sections.abstract: A reinforcement-learning platform generated neuraminidase-targeting molecules; two selected compounds inhibited influenza A/B in enzyme and cell assays and showed activity in mice.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report two compounds with cell-assay EC50 values of 0.29–2.31 μM and 65–100% protection in the reported mouse infection groups; groups had six mice each.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an accepted manuscript of a 2024 article, not new 2026 experimental work. Evidence is preclinical; the compounds were tested at higher doses than oseltamivir and no human efficacy or safety is established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.BM listing; peer-reviewed publication is identified in the arXiv record (Antiviral Research, 2024; DOI 10.1016/j.antiviral.2024.105818), with enzyme, cell, and mouse evidence.

sections.title: Rule-based curation and validation in batch fermentation of a genome-scale metabolic model of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5
sections.abstract: The authors built the iJL1143 genome-scale metabolic model for Fusarium venenatum A3/5 and compared it with a draft model in four oxygen-enriched glucose/fructose batch fermentations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that curation reduced mean final-biomass discrepancy from 20% to 6%; adding a fitted lag time reduced biomass time-course error from 4.88 to 0.42 g/L.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation covers one strain, oxygen-enriched batch conditions, and the tested substrates; transfer to other feedstocks or industrial conditions remains unshown.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.MN listing and comparison with four fermentation experiments; reported biomass discrepancies are quantitative and tied to measured batch runs.

sections.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
sections.abstract: OCCAM combines denoising-based cell representations with gene-interaction, text, and protein-sequence features to predict genetic-perturbation responses across contexts and gene combinations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved perturbation-pattern matching over four retrained competitors or transfer baselines, and better double-perturbation estimates than summed single effects.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says expression-level prediction remains challenging; these are computational benchmark results, not evidence of patient or therapeutic effects.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: q-bio.QM listing and cross-listing in AI/ML; evaluated on cross-context few-shot settings, held-out cell lines, multiple assays, and double perturbations.

sections.title: ST-FateFlow: Continuous Gene-Spatial Reconstruction with Differentiation-Potential Learning from Time-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomics
sections.abstract: ST-FateFlow uses structure-aware transport coupling and flow matching to infer continuous gene-expression and spatial dynamics between unpaired spatial-transcriptomic snapshots.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved expression-distribution and spatial interpolation metrics and differentiation-associated orderings consistent with previously described trajectories.
sections.unique_caveat: It reconstructs missing states from public data rather than measuring lineage transitions; results depend on cross-time coupling, registration, and missing-state assumptions. The learned potential is not a fate probability or physical energy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.GN listing; tested computationally across three public developmental and regenerative spatial-transcriptomics datasets.

sections.title: Deep Learning-based Multiparametric Quantitative Ultrasound for Hepatic Steatosis Assessment
sections.abstract: A U-Net combines quantitative-ultrasound maps to estimate spatially resolved liver fat fraction against MRI-PDFF measurements.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that H-scan, attenuation, and Nakagami inputs performed best, with Spearman correlation 0.92 and AUC 0.98 in this cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: The cohort is small and severe steatosis underrepresented; the authors call for larger, more diverse validation and direct assessment across liver lobes. This is not a validated screening or diagnostic test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Replacement revision in the 2026-11-18 batch; evaluated on ultrasound data from 30 people with healthy, suspected, or confirmed MASLD and compared with MRI-PDFF.

sections.title: Diversity Preservation Recovers Transcription Factor Motifs Across Challenging Confounder Landscapes
sections.abstract: The study combines evolvable motif length with MAP-Elites diversity archives to recover transcription-factor motifs despite confounding sequences.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that every MAP-Elites archive ranked the target first in at least 13 of 30 seeds per dataset, while the baseline never did so across three datasets.
sections.unique_caveat: Motif attribution remains difficult: HNF4A and JUND were not consistently ranked above close relatives across the full motif-width range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: q-bio.GN cross-list and evaluation on five liver ChIP-seq datasets, with comparisons against a survivor-selection baseline and MEME on the same sequences.

sections.title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
sections.abstract: HoloGene uses an anisotropic conditional implicit neural representation to infer continuous three-dimensional gene-expression fields from pre-registered spatial-transcriptomics sections.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved reconstruction accuracy and biological-preservation metrics versus general-purpose implicit representations and spatial-transcriptomics baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: Unsampled tissue is inferred, not observed; the result depends on registration, sampling density, and the held-out-section evaluation design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: q-bio.GN cross-list; the arXiv record notes NeurIPS 2026, and the paper evaluates against held-out measured sections and adapted baselines.

sections.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
sections.abstract: An analysis of resting-state EEG shows how null-network construction and hub selection can change whether a rich-club group difference appears.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that one of four pipelines produced an apparent group difference and did so in 43% of empirical pseudo-studies, while the other three were near the expected 5% rate.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small EEG methodology case study, not molecular evidence or a diagnostic result; conclusions depend on the question each null model is designed to test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted-manuscript replacement in the batch; the arXiv record links a Journal of Neuroscience Methods article and DOI 10.1016/j.jneumeth.2026.110927; analysis uses 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls.

sections.title: Molecular memory reduces timing noise in stochastic gene expression
sections.abstract: Analytical calculations and stochastic simulations suggest that multistep mRNA production and degradation can reduce first-passage-time noise through different mechanisms.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive small-noise-limit statistics and report simulation support, including qualitative persistence beyond that approximation's regime.
sections.unique_caveat: This is theoretical/model-based work with no biochemical or cellular experiment reported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.MN listing and a mechanistic link between RNA processing assumptions and timing variability in gene-expression models.

sections.title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
sections.abstract: A cardinality-optimisation framework allocates recruitment and metabolomic samples across sites while balancing yield, cost, capacity, and logistics.
sections.claimed_contribution: In simulated multi-centre scenarios for a project targeting 1,900 diagnosed patients, the authors report maintained feasibility under tighter constraints and about 30% lower metabolomic-analysis cost in unconstrained comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is simulation and operational modelling; it does not show improved recruitment in a completed study or better patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.QM listing and an explicit rare-disease study-design application spanning 24 centres and eight metabolomic laboratories.

sections.title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
sections.abstract: The authors derive conditions under which biochemical feedback and resource competition change expression dynamics without reversing cumulative-dose ordering in incoherent feedforward-loop models.
sections.claimed_contribution: At one fixed joint fit, the authors report decreasing cumulative output over a 20–100 ng burden range, while showing that preserved ordering does not imply equal quantitative response.
sections.unique_caveat: The quantitative example is model- and fit-specific; the result is not experimental confirmation of a general biological law.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.MN listing; combines mathematical comparison bounds with two fitted model examples involving translation blocking and RNA decay.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Sparse-measurement reconstruction, AI-assisted prediction linked to biological measurements, robust inference under confounding, and mechanistic modeling recur in this selected batch.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: The selected papers support prospective validation of reconstructed spatial dynamics, transfer tests for fermentation and ultrasound models, independent replication of AI-generated biology proposals, and cohort replication for EEG pipeline sensitivity.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The batch is led by computational biology that predicts perturbations or fills gaps in sparse measurements, but its strongest empirical anchors remain bounded cell, fermentation, ultrasound-cohort, and previously published mouse studies.
